title: SSE reconnect heuristics and ambiguous fragment repair
creator: Avery Chen
description: Several hosted customers reported truncated or duplicated streaming responses after network blips and autoscaler-driven connection handoffs. Root cause appears to be ambiguity when clients reconnect with a stale Last-Event-ID or without an explicit resume token while the server has rotated ephemeral session metadata during autoscale. The server currently attempts a best-effort stitch of fragments which leads to duplicate tokens, missing tail tokens, or hanging partial outputs when fragments overlap or server checkpoints are evicted.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running generation via hosted SSE (customer example uses max_tokens=1200).
2) Kill the TCP connection mid-stream to simulate a network blip (SIGTERM on client).
3) Allow server autoscaler to shift the session (scale-up) and evict ephemeral checkpoint within 30-90s window.

4) Client attempts reconnect: a) with Last-Event-ID header set to last received offset, b) without resume-token header. Observe either duplicated token sequence or missing final tokens in the rebuilt stream.
5) Reproduce at scale by running 200 concurrent clients and toggling blip timing relative to autoscaler events to surface race conditions.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Pager alert triggered by two customers (AcmePayments, NotesAI) reporting content truncation after reconnects (Slack logs #prod-escalations).

2026-03-11: Core dump & trace captured from runtime node 5c2; trace shows session checkpoint TTL expired during autoscale reconciliation (artifact: s3://redwood-prod-artifacts/trace-5c2-20260311.log).
2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with deterministic client harness by advancing system clock to force checkpoint eviction (see repro harness: github.com/redwood/repro/sse-resume-harness).

2026-03-12: Observability shows 0.7% increase in 'partial_stream' alerts; correlated with autoscaler activity windows 02:00-04:00 UTC for EMEA region (Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-health).

Notes: existing resume logic uses Last-Event-ID string + best-effort chunk overlap removal. This is brittle when server fragment boundaries change or when the server applies a rotation to ephemeral session ids.
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce an explicit resume token (opaque 64-bit anchor) emitted periodically in SSE frames (every 32 tokens) and included in final event metadata. The token encodes stable sequence anchor and server epoch.

2) Server-side: maintain a sliding reconciliation window of recent fragments (configurable, default 1024 tokens) associated with resume tokens. When a reconnect occurs with a resume token mismatch but overlapping Last-Event-ID, attempt deterministic backfill using anchor-based alignment instead of naive overlap trimming.

3) Add a /stream/backfill endpoint for clients to request missing tokens between last-known anchor and latest anchor (authenticated, short TTL). This avoids guessing via SSE replays and gives clients a canonical repair path.

4) Short-term mitigation: temporarily extend ephemeral checkpoint TTL during autoscaler handoffs (config flag autoscale.checkpoint_ttl -> 120s) and toggle to rollout only in hosted clusters while backfill feature is implemented.
5) Client SDK: add automatic resend of a Resume-Token header when reconnecting; fallback to Last-Event-ID only if token absent. Ship patches to JS/Python SDKs as hotfixes.
rollout_plan: Phase A (hotfix): Increase checkpoint TTL and deploy TTL change to hosted clusters (canary in us-west-2) - target: 2026-03-15.
Phase B (server): Implement resume-token emission + reconciliation window; add comprehensive unit/integration tests; internal canary with synthetic load - target merge: 2026-03-20.
Phase C (client): Ship SDK patches (js v1.4.3, py v1.4.3) that prefer Resume-Token header - target publish: 2026-03-22.
Phase D (feature): Deploy /stream/backfill and enable for affected customers behind feature flag; monitor partial_stream alerts for 72h - target: 2026-03-29.
Rollback: TTL hotfix can be reverted instantly via feature flag; resume-token rollout is backwards compatible as token is additive.
qa_checks: Automated unit tests for token anchor generation and deterministic alignment logic.
Integration test: inject blip at various token offsets and verify idempotent reconstruction (no duplicates, no missing tokens) across 1000 runs.
Chaos test: simulate autoscaler-driven node rotation while many clients reconnect; assert <0.1% partial_stream rate compared to baseline.
Manual verify with customer repro payloads (AcmePayments / NotesAI) before and after backfill endpoint enabled.
Observability: create Grafana alerts for partial_stream rate, resume_token_mismatch_count, and backfill_success_ratio.
